name: Job Seeking Visa
description: The D-10 visa allows qualified individuals to stay in Korea while actively searching for employment. It's ideal for recent graduates from Korean universities or professionals seeking career opportunities.
tagline: Your gateway to a Korean career
targetAudience: Former E-7 visa holders between jobs

eligibility.label: Graduated from a Korean university (Associate's degree or higher)
Bachelor's degree or higher from accredited foreign university
Relevant professional experience in specialized field
TOPIK Level 4 or higher (bonus, not required)

fees.notes: Fees may vary; check HiKorea for current rates

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must be valid for at least 6 months beyond intended stay

documents.name: Visa Application Form
documents.where_to_get: Download from HiKorea or get at immigration office

documents.name: Passport Photo
documents.description: 3.5cm x 4.5cm, taken within last 6 months, white background

documents.name: Degree Certificate
documents.description: Original or certified copy of your highest degree
tips: Must be apostilled or authenticated if from foreign country

documents.name: Job Search Plan
documents.description: Document outlining your job search strategy and target companies
tips: Include specific companies you plan to apply to
Show you've researched the Korean job market

documents.name: Bank Statement
documents.description: Proof of sufficient funds for your stay

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Documents
applicationSteps.description: Gather all required documents. Get foreign documents apostilled or authenticated.
tips: Start early - apostille can take time

applicationSteps.title: Book Appointment
applicationSteps.description: Schedule an appointment at your local immigration office via HiKorea.
tips: Book early - popular offices fill up quickly

applicationSteps.title: Submit Application
applicationSteps.description: Visit the immigration office with all documents. Submit application and pay fee.

applicationSteps.title: Wait for Processing
applicationSteps.description: Application is reviewed. You may be contacted for additional documents.

applicationSteps.title: Receive Result
applicationSteps.description: Pick up your visa or ARC card, or receive notification of result.

processingTime.notes: May vary based on immigration office workload and completeness of application

restrictions: Must get prior approval from immigration
workPermission.notes: Full-time work requires changing to appropriate work visa (E-7, etc.)

faqs.question: Can I work while on a D-10 visa?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only part-time (up to 20 hours per week) with prior approval from immigration. You must obtain a part-time work permit.

faqs.question: How do I extend my D-10 visa?
faqs.answer: Visit immigration 30 days before expiration with proof of active job searching (applications sent, interviews attended, etc.). You can extend up to a maximum of 2 years total.

faqs.question: What happens when I find a job?
faqs.answer: You'll need to change your status to an appropriate work visa (usually E-7). Your employer will help sponsor this visa change.

faqs.question: Can I study Korean while on D-10?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can enroll in Korean language courses. This doesn't count against your work hours.

tips: Start job searching before your current visa expires
Network actively - many Korean jobs are filled through connections
Learn Korean - even basic proficiency greatly improves your chances
Keep detailed records of your job search activities for extension
Join expat job boards and LinkedIn groups focused on Korea
Consider working with a recruitment agency specializing in foreign talent
warnings: Don't overstay your visa - it severely impacts future visa applications
Working full-time without proper authorization is illegal
Always carry your ARC card when outside
